# Acts of Thomas — Chapter 2
**Agent:** EMET (Literal)
**Source:** Syriac MS / Greek recension, Acts of Thomas 2

---

*[Thomas arrives in India. The king's wedding banquet. The flute-girl. Thomas sings.]*

1. And the merchant Abbanes took Judas and they went together to a certain city of India where a great feast was being made, for the king of that city had an only daughter, and she was being given in marriage.

2. And the king had caused it to be proclaimed throughout all the city that all men should come to his daughter's wedding feast.

3. And Abbanes also went with Thomas to the feast.

4. And Thomas reclined and they all ate and drank.

5. And a Hebrew flute-girl was there, who played the flute before them. And she went round to each one playing, and when she came to Thomas she played the flute over him for a long time.

6. Now that flute-girl was of the Hebrew race, and Thomas spoke to her in Hebrew.

7. And she loved him greatly and was held fast by him, and she left off playing to all the others and was always near Thomas and played before him.

8. But the cup-bearer of the king came and smote Thomas on the cheek and said: "Play for the others also, not for this one only!"

9. And Thomas looked at him and said: "My God will forgive this smiting in the world to come, but in this world he will show his wonders, and I shall see that hand which smote me dragged by dogs."

10. And after a certain time the cup-bearer went out to draw water from the well, and a lion struck him down and killed him; and the dogs dragged him, and one of the dogs, a black one, brought his right hand into the banqueting hall.

11. And when they saw it they all marveled, and inquired who it was that had prophesied this.

12. And the flute-girl broke her flute and sat down at Thomas's feet, saying: "Either this man is God or God's apostle. For I heard him speak Hebrew, and I came and sat beside him; and now I have seen what he has done."

---
*EMET note: The Syriac *qinayta* (flute-girl / lament-singer) is specifically a Jewish professional mourner-musician. Her Hebrew speech marks her as diaspora Jewish — creating a bond of identity with Thomas. The cup-bearer's instantaneous judgment (killed by lion, hand brought by dog) is the first miracle in the ATH.*
